fields.design: Owner rule: a ticker's history belongs to <managed sector>/<TICKER> (the scheduled forecast/review store); no managed entry, no sector or conflicting entries -> no owner, nothing guessed. store_inventory (new, read-only CLI, never constructs a PredictionStore): per store identity + digest, file kinds, files_by_roster (exact match of dimension keys to each graph's AGENT_WEIGHTS), declared sectors (feedback/weights/ledger never evidence), status confirmed|conflicting|directory_only|roster_only|missing|empty, ownership (role, roster_vs_owner, registry_agrees), schema markers, consumer classes; duplicates: tickers, envelope cycle ids, graded days, identical|conflicting; sanitized; digest excludes generated_at. store_migration (new CLI): plan (read-only, digest over items/holds/flags/managed sha) quarantines non-canonical non-empty stores of managed tickers, holds unmanaged duplicates, owner/map conflicts, sectorless/conflicting entries and case-variant owner stores, flags owner stores with another roster; apply --approve <digest> recomputes, new migration dir + lineage.json, per-store re-hash immediately before one directory rename into data/prediction_quarantine/<id>/stores/, re-hash after; rollback renames back after verifying, refuses a reappeared live store or a changed quarantine. Writers: server._self_heal_rl uses each managed entry's sector (looked in automobile/<TICKER> for every ticker); PredictionStore stamps its own sector on created logs, weight memory and ledgers (old files untouched); daily_review rebuilds missing weights from get_sector_weights(sector), live and paper.

implementation.summary: core/ops/error_backlog.py groups telemetry.db app_logs WARNING+ rows into issues by a deterministic fingerprint (sha256 of source, logger and a normalised template: pre-E1 prefix, timestamps, ids incl. Atlas user ids, numbers (HTTP/status_code/Errno codes kept), paths, URL paths/queries (host kept), quoted values, secrets and symbols removed; tracebacks reduced to exception type and message; no LLM). Severity = app_logs.level; Railway's stderr envelope is never an input (railway_occurrences reads the app's own level offline). Lifecycle: new/ongoing/quiet/regressed + spiking flag; triage open/acknowledged/fixed/wontfix with assignee/task/note; fixed reopens on a later occurrence, acknowledged regresses after a 7-day quiet gap; a fix is verified only when archive coverage passes fixed_at+7d, else unobserved. Tables error_issues + error_backlog_cursor in telemetry.db on the module's own connection; cursor batches in BEGIN IMMEDIATE (no double count across workers) plus a process lock (shared connection in the thread pool); max 20,000 rows per read. Retention bounded (30 daily counts, 20 run ids/tickers, 90-day prune of unprotected issues, 2,000 cap that never drops an active issue); app_logs never changed. Deterministic digest. services/api/routes/ops_api.py: GET /ops/errors, GET /ops/errors/digest, POST /ops/errors/{fp} (require_owner). Watchdog check error_backlog registered in checks.py but in no milestones.yaml entry (sends nothing; test pins). Dead letters consumed via the outbox's per-row WARNING. scripts/prod_errors.py (app credentials only; offline --db / --railway-json). config.yaml error_backlog section.

fields.sequencing_note: Owner decision 2026-10-29: placed directly after FIX-016, ahead of SA-048. PR-009's push now waits for FIX-016 and FIX-018, and the three go out in one push at the owner's word, so the gate is fixed before any shadow row exists. Rule: a decision with a lasting no-result (an empty NSE list read as such, a list starting after the close, a bonus or split ex by the review day, an unread share-count row, two ratios on one day, a change no ratio converts or a row of no known kind between the closes, a registry basis change) is set aside at both horizons and named on the scorecard; at most 2 decisions and 10% of those past 30 sessions, beyond which the gate says 'cannot judge' (never a pass). Temporary gaps (a failed read, no close, a Yahoo-only close) still count as not right and fail the week. The 15-decision minimum counts the decisions not set aside. Offered as about 1 point; 2 because grading must also tell a failed fetch from an empty list (fetch_corp_actions returns [] for both).
